## R Markdown
```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

nsw_shellfish <- st_read("raw_data/NSW/NSW_aquaculture_leases_2025/Aquaculture_Leases.shp") |>
   st_transform(3577)  # GDA94 / Australian Albers for area in m²

nsw_shellfish$area_m2 <- as.numeric(st_area(nsw_shellfish))

summary(nsw_shellfish$area_m2)
quantile(nsw_shellfish$area_m2, c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95))
```

```{r}
ggplot(nsw_shellfish, aes(x = area_m2)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#4C72B0", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = pi * 50^2, colour = "#C44E52", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = pi * 50^2, y = Inf, 
           label = "50 m buffer\n(7,854 m²)", 
           hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5, colour = "#C44E52") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "Lease area (m², log scale)", y = "Number of leases",
       title = "NSW aquaculture lease areas vs. 50 m buffer footprint") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#sensitivity mention: because the distribution is skewed, the buffer under-represents the upper quartile of leases. Whether this matters depends on what you're using the buffered areas for — if it's national infrastructure accounting, you could note that total buffered area will be a conservative estimate of true national shellfish lease extent.

```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(here)

# Read data using here()
nsw_shellfish <- st_read(here("raw_data", "NSW", 
                              "NSW_aquaculture_leases_2025",
                              "Aquaculture_Leases.shp")) |>
  st_transform(3577)

nsw_shellfish$area_m2 <- as.numeric(st_area(nsw_shellfish))

# Validation figure
buffer_area <- pi * 50^2           # 7,854 m²
median_area <- median(nsw_shellfish$area_m2)

# Place labels at different heights using absolute y-positions
# and move them to opposite sides so they don't overlap each other
y_max <- max(ggplot_build(
  ggplot(nsw_shellfish, aes(x = area_m2)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
    scale_x_log10()
)$data[[1]]$count)

fig_validation <- ggplot(nsw_shellfish, aes(x = area_m2)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#0072B2", colour = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = buffer_area, colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median_area, colour = "#009E73",
             linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  # 50 m buffer label: right side of its line, upper area
  annotate("text", x = buffer_area * 1.8, y = y_max * 0.95,
           label = paste0("50 m buffer\n(", comma(round(buffer_area)), " m²)"),
           hjust = 0, colour = "#D55E00", size = 3.2, lineheight = 0.9) +
  # Median label: left side of its line, slightly lower
  annotate("text", x = median_area / 1.8, y = y_max * 0.75,
           label = paste0("Median lease\n(", comma(round(median_area)), " m²)"),
           hjust = 1, colour = "#009E73", size = 3.2, lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma,
                breaks = c(100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 1000000),
                expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.08))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = expression("Lease area (m"^2*", log"[10]*" scale)"),
       y = "Number of leases",
       caption = paste0("NSW marine shellfish leases (n = ",
                        nrow(nsw_shellfish), "). Source: NSW DPI, 2025.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey40", size = 8),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
fig_validation

# Save — here() wraps ONLY the path, then other args come after
ggsave(here("figures", "SI_buffer_validation.png"),
       plot = fig_validation,
       width = 17, height = 10, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```
```{r}
nsw_shellfish |>
  mutate(area_m2 = as.numeric(st_area(st_transform(geometry, 3577)))) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_below_100m2 = sum(area_m2 < 100),
    n_above_100000m2 = sum(area_m2 > 100000)
  )
```

```{r}
nsw_shellfish |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_below_100m2 = sum(area_m2 < 100),
    n_above_100000m2 = sum(area_m2 > 100000)
  )
```
